prompt: A hospital's revenue per patient fell 9% while patient numbers held steady. The share of patients on government insurance rose from 30% to 45%. Which is the strongest initial hypothesis?

options.text: Rivals are likely drawing patients away from the hospital.
Payer mix, coding, services and billing probably contribute.
options.feedback: This lists causes without committing to one.

options.text: Private insurers likely cut their rates more than usual.
options.feedback: Possible, but nothing points to it. The 15-point shift to government payers can explain a 9% drop on its own if they pay about half as much.

options.text: Lower-paying government insurance likely explains the 9% drop.
options.feedback: Right. A 15-point shift toward lower-paying government insurance can explain a 9% drop. I'd compare revenue per patient by payer type.

explanation: The data shows patients steady, revenue per patient down 9%, and government insurance rising from 30% to 45% of patients. Likely cause: the shift to lower-paying government insurance. To test it, compare revenue per patient by payer type. If each payer's revenue per patient also fell, look at coding or services.
